title: Wearable Ankle Power Training (WearAPT) for Enhanced Mobility in Aging
official: Wearable Ankle Power Training (WearAPT) for Enhanced Mobility in Aging
summary: This project introduces and investigates the scientific premise that passive wearable therapeutic devices can enhance plantarflexor muscle performance during walking to elicit and promote lasting physiological and functional improvements for older adults. The investigators aim to quantify the preliminary efficacy of wearable plantarflexor resistance training to enhance gait performance in older adults, investigate neural and muscular mechanisms of adaptation, and identify target candidate characteristics for personalized treatment strategies. The investigators will test the hypothesis that, compared to baseline and unlike controls, WearAPT will increase peak ankle power output, stride length, habitual and maximum walking speeds, walking economy, and 6-min walk distance.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* insufficient weekly physical activity levels (i.e., ≤150 minutes moderate-intensity or ≤75 minutes vigorous-intensity activity)
* self-select a habitual walking speed deemed indicative of age-related slowing (i.e., ≤1.1 m/s)
* self-report at least some physical ability limitations (i.e., ≥4 on the "Stay Independent" questionnaire).

Exclusion Criteria:

* leg injury or fracture within the last 6 months
* diagnosed anemia
* neurological disorder of the legs such as peripheral neuropathy
* vascular disorder of the legs such as peripheral arterial disease
* taking medication that causes dizziness
* cannot walk without an assistive aid (i.e., cane or walker)
* Mini Mental State Exam ≤25
